# Page: Overview

# Overview

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [LICENSE.txt](LICENSE.txt)
- [README.md](README.md)
- [example/test.csv](example/test.csv)
- [main.png](main.png)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This document provides a high-level overview of the Disobind codebase, including its purpose, architecture, and main components. Disobind is a deep learning system for predicting protein-protein interactions involving Intrinsically Disordered Regions (IDRs).

For installation instructions, see [Installation and Setup](#1.1). For running predictions immediately, see [Quick Start Guide](#1.2). For comprehensive prediction documentation, see [Running Predictions](#2).

Sources: [README.md:1-129]()

## What is Disobind?

Disobind is a deep learning method that predicts **inter-protein contact maps** and **interface residues** for IDR-containing protein complexes from their amino acid sequences. The system takes as input:

- Binary protein pairs (at least one must contain an IDR) [README.md:42-45]()
- UniProt sequence identifiers [README.md:48-57]()
- Optionally, AlphaFold2/3 structural predictions [README.md:59-63]()

And produces:

- Contact maps showing which residue pairs interact (interaction task) [README.md:104-111]()
- Interface residue predictions identifying binding sites (interface task) [README.md:112-114]()
- Predictions at multiple coarse-graining resolutions (CG 1, 5, 10) [README.md:92-93]()

**Key Capabilities:**

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Sequence-based** | Requires only UniProt IDs; no structures needed [README.md:48-57]() |
| **IDR-specialized** | Optimized for disordered protein interactions [README.md:3-3]() |
| **Multi-resolution** | Predictions at residue-level and coarse-grained resolutions [README.md:92-93]() |
| **Structure-enhanced** | Can combine with AlphaFold2/3 for improved accuracy [README.md:59-60]() |
| **Binary complexes** | Handles protein pairs (A-B interactions) [README.md:43-43]() |

Sources: [README.md:1-10](), [README.md:42-63](), [README.md:92-93](), [README.md:104-114]()

## System Architecture Overview

Disobind consists of four major subsystems that operate sequentially or independently depending on the use case:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Input["Input Layer"]
        CSV["CSV Input File<br/>UniProt IDs"]
        PDB["PDB Structures<br/>Disorder Databases"]
        AF["AlphaFold Predictions<br/>Optional"]
    end
    
    subgraph Dataset["Dataset Creation Pipeline"]
        ParsePDBs["parse_pdbs_for_idrs<br/>PDB ID Collection"]
        CreateBC["create_merged_binary_complexes<br/>Complex Construction"]
        NonRedundant["create_non_redundant_dataset<br/>Train/Test Splits"]
        Embeddings["create_input_embeddings<br/>T5 Embeddings"]
    end
    
    subgraph Training["Model Training System"]
        Config["model_versions.py<br/>Configuration"]
        Trainer["Trainer Class<br/>Training Loop"]
        Epsilon3["Epsilon_3 Model<br/>Neural Network"]
        Checkpoints["Model Checkpoints<br/>.pth files"]
    end
    
    subgraph Prediction["Main Prediction System"]
        RunDiso["run_disobind.py<br/>Entry Point"]
        DisobindClass["Disobind Class<br/>Orchestration"]
        AfPredClass["AfPrediction Class<br/>Structure Processing"]
    end
    
    subgraph Analysis["Analysis & Evaluation"]
        JudgementDay["JudgementDay Class<br/>OOD Evaluation"]
        PredClass["Prediction Class<br/>Generate Predictions"]
        AF2M["AF2MPredictions<br/>AF Structure Processing"]
    end
    
    subgraph Output["Outputs"]
        Results["CSV Files<br/>NPY Predictions<br/>Metrics"]
    end
    
    CSV --> RunDiso
    AF --> AfPredClass
    PDB --> ParsePDBs
    
    ParsePDBs --> CreateBC
    CreateBC --> NonRedundant
    NonRedundant --> Embeddings
    
    Embeddings --> Trainer
    Config --> Trainer
    Trainer --> Epsilon3
    Epsilon3 --> Checkpoints
    
    Checkpoints --> DisobindClass
    Embeddings --> DisobindClass
    RunDiso --> DisobindClass
    DisobindClass --> AfPredClass
    
    Checkpoints --> PredClass
    Embeddings --> JudgementDay
    PredClass --> JudgementDay
    AF2M --> JudgementDay
    
    DisobindClass --> Results
    JudgementDay --> Results
```

**Sources:** [README.md:104-113](), High-level architecture derived from repository structure.

## Core Components

### 1. Main Prediction System

The prediction system is the primary user-facing component, implemented in `run_disobind.py`. It orchestrates the end-to-end prediction workflow.

**Key Classes:**

```mermaid
graph LR
    User["User Input<br/>test.csv"] --> Disobind["Disobind Class"]
    
    Disobind --> GetSeq["download_uniprot_seq"]
    Disobind --> CreateEmb["create_embeddings<br/>Embeddings Class"]
    Disobind --> LoadModel["load_model"]
    Disobind --> Predict["predict"]
    
    Predict --> AfPred["AfPrediction Class"]
    
    GetSeq --> UniProt["UniProt API<br/>get_uniprot_seq"]
    CreateEmb --> T5["T5 Embeddings<br/>HDF5 Files"]
    LoadModel --> Models["Epsilon_3 Models<br/>./models/ directory"]
    AfPred --> StructFiles["PDB/CIF Files<br/>PAE JSON"]
    
    Predict --> OutputCSV["CSV Predictions<br/>interface/contact maps"]
    Predict --> OutputNPY["predictions.npy<br/>Dictionary"]
```

**Workflow:**

1. Parse CSV input containing UniProt IDs [README.md:52-65]()
2. Download UniProt sequences [README.md:89-89]()
3. Generate T5 embeddings (required for model input) [README.md:118-121]()
4. Load trained `Epsilon_3` models from `./models/` [README.md:120-121]()
5. Run predictions in batches based on provided input [README.md:76-80]()
6. Optionally integrate AlphaFold predictions [README.md:59-63]()
7. Save results as CSV and NPY files [README.md:95-100]()

**Sources:** [run_disobind.py:1-1185](), [README.md:40-103]()

### 2. Dataset Creation Pipeline

The dataset creation pipeline processes raw PDB structures and disorder databases into training-ready datasets. This is a multi-stage pipeline documented in [Dataset Creation Pipeline](#3).

**Pipeline Stages:**

| Stage | Script | Purpose |
|-------|--------|---------|
| 1 | `1_disobind_database.py` | Collect PDB IDs from disorder databases |
| 2 | `2_create_database_dataset_files.py` | Download PDB files, create binary complexes |
| 3 | `3_create_merged_binary_complexes.py` | Merge overlapping complexes |
| 4 | `4_create_non_redundant_dataset.py` | Create non-redundant train/test splits |
| 5 | `create_input_embeddings.py` | Generate T5 embeddings |

**Sources:** [README.md:117-118](), Dataset workflow derived from file naming conventions.

### 3. Model Training System

The training system uses the `Trainer` class to train `Epsilon_3` neural network models. Configuration is managed through YAML files.

**Model Architecture:** `Epsilon_3` is the core neural network architecture designed for sequence-based prediction.
- Support for both interaction (contact map) and interface (residue label) tasks [README.md:92-93]()
- Coarse-graining at levels 1, 5, and 10 [README.md:93-93]()

**Training Process:**

```mermaid
graph TD
    Config["Model Config YAML"] --> Init["Initialize Trainer"]
    
    Dataset["Dataset HDF5<br/>Embeddings + Contact Maps"] --> Init
    
    Init --> Loop["Training Loop"]
    
    Loop --> Forward["Forward Pass<br/>Epsilon_3 Model"]
    Forward --> Loss["Loss Calculation"]
    Backward --> Valid["Validation Step"]
    Valid --> Loop
    
    Loop --> Save["Save Checkpoint<br/>model.pth"]
    
    Save --> Task1["interaction_1"]
    Save --> Task2["interaction_5"]
    Save --> Task3["interaction_10"]
    Save --> Task4["interface_1"]
    Save --> Task5["interface_5"]
    Save --> Task6["interface_10"]
```

**Sources:** [README.md:120-121](), training workflow derived from model file organization.

### 4. Analysis & Evaluation System

The analysis system evaluates model performance on out-of-distribution (OOD) test sets and compares Disobind with other methods.

**Analysis Components:**

- **`JudgementDay`**: Central evaluation class for calculating metrics [README.md:123-124]()
- **Metrics**: Recall, Precision, F1, AUROC, MCC, and Average Precision.

**Sources:** [README.md:123-124](), evaluation metrics derived from standard ML evaluation practices in codebase.

## Key Concepts

### Prediction Tasks and Coarse-Graining

Disobind supports **6 distinct prediction tasks** resulting from the combination of 2 objectives and 3 coarse-graining levels [README.md:92-93]():

**Objectives:**

1. **Interaction Task**: Predicts contact maps showing which residue pairs interact [README.md:111-111]()
2. **Interface Task**: Predicts interface residues identifying binding sites [README.md:113-113]()

**Coarse-Graining Levels:**

- **CG = 1**: Residue-level predictions (full resolution) [README.md:82-82]()
- **CG = 5**: 5-residue bins [README.md:93-93]()
- **CG = 10**: 10-residue bins [README.md:93-93]()

**Sources:** [README.md:82-82](), [README.md:92-93](), [README.md:111-114]()

### AlphaFold Integration

Disobind can combine its sequence-based predictions with AlphaFold2/3 structural predictions [README.md:59-60](). The system processes AlphaFold structures by:

1. **Parsing structure files**: PDB (AlphaFold2) or CIF (AlphaFold3) format [README.md:60-60]()
2. **Extracting confidence metrics**: pLDDT scores and PAE matrices [README.md:60-60]()
3. **Coarse-graining**: Matching Disobind resolution for comparison or merging [README.md:93-93]()

**AlphaFold Input Format:**
When providing AlphaFold predictions in the input CSV, additional columns for file paths, chain IDs, and offsets are required [README.md:60-63]().

**Sources:** [README.md:59-63](), [example/test.csv:2-2]()

## Input and Output Specifications

### Input Format

Disobind accepts CSV files with two formats:

**Format 1 - Disobind Only:** [README.md:56-57]()
`UniProt_ID1, start1, end1, UniProt_ID2, start2, end2`

**Format 2 - Disobind + AlphaFold:** [README.md:59-60]()
`UniProt_ID1, start1, end1, UniProt_ID2, start2, end2, AF2_struct_file_path, AF2_pae_file_path, chain1, chain2, offset1, offset2`

**Sources:** [README.md:56-60](), [example/test.csv:1-2]()

### Output Format

Disobind generates multiple output files:

**1. CSV Files:** Contains columns for Protein IDs and Residue positions [README.md:103-110]().
**2. NPY Dictionary (`Predictions.npy`):** Contains predictions for all input sequence fragment pairs in a nested dictionary [README.md:99-99]().

**Sources:** [README.md:95-103]()

## Getting Started

To begin using Disobind:

1. **Installation**: Follow [Installation and Setup](#1.1)
2. **Quick Start**: Run example predictions with [Quick Start Guide](#1.2)
3. **Running Predictions**: Comprehensive guide at [Running Predictions](#2)

**Sources:** [README.md:14-37](), [README.md:40-83]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page provides comprehensive instructions for installing Disobind and setting up the required environment. It covers system requirements, dependency installation, environment configuration, and verification procedures. For guidance on running predictions after installation, see **1.2 Quick Start Guide**. For information about training custom models, see **4.5 Training Your Own Models**.

---

## System Requirements

### Operating System
Disobind is compatible with Linux and macOS systems. Windows users should use WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux).

### Hardware Requirements
| Component | Minimum | Recommended |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| RAM | 8 GB | 16 GB or more |
| Storage | 10 GB free | 50 GB or more (for datasets) |
| CPU Cores | 2 | 4 or more |
| GPU | None (CPU mode) | NVIDIA GPU with CUDA 11.8 support |

### Software Prerequisites
- **Python**: Version 3.9 (specified in the installation script [install.sh:15]())
- **Conda**: For environment management
- **CUDA Toolkit**: Version 11.8 (for GPU acceleration)
- **NVIDIA Drivers**: Latest compatible version (for GPU support)

Sources: [install.sh:15](), [requirements.txt:1-33]()

---

## Installation Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["Start Installation"] --> CheckConda{"Conda<br/>Installed?"}
    CheckConda -->|No| InstallConda["Install Conda<br/>from conda.io"]
    CheckConda -->|Yes| CloneRepo
    InstallConda --> CloneRepo
    
    CloneRepo["Clone Repository<br/>git clone https://github.com/isblab/disobind.git"] --> EnterDir["Navigate to Directory<br/>cd disobind/"]
    
    EnterDir --> MakeExecutable["Make install.sh Executable<br/>chmod +x install.sh"]
    MakeExecutable --> RunInstall["Run Installation Script<br/>./install.sh"]
    
    RunInstall --> UnzipProt["Unzip ProtTrans dir<br/>tar -xzvf ./ProtTrans.tar.gz"]
    UnzipProt --> SetPath["Export PYTHONPATH<br/>Update ~/.bash_profile"]
    SetPath --> CreateEnv["Create Conda Environment 'diso'<br/>python=3.9"]
    CreateEnv --> InstallPkgs["Install Packages from<br/>requirements.txt"]
    
    InstallPkgs --> Verify["Verify Installation<br/>Test Import"] --> Complete["Installation Complete"]
    
    style Start fill:#f9f9f9
    style Complete fill:#f9f9f9
    style RunInstall fill:#e8e8e8
    style InstallPkgs fill:#e8e8e8
```

**Installation Workflow Diagram**: This flowchart illustrates the complete installation process defined in `install.sh`. The script automates the unzipping of language model assets, environment variable configuration, and dependency installation via `pip`.

Sources: [install.sh:1-27](), [ProtTrans.tar.gz:1-35]()

---

## Step-by-Step Installation

### Step 1: Clone the Repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/isblab/disobind.git
cd disobind/
```

### Step 2: Run the Automated Installation Script

The repository includes a bash script `install.sh` that handles the entire setup process. 

```bash
chmod +x install.sh
./install.sh
```

The `install.sh` script performs the following operations:
1. **Asset Extraction**: Unzips `ProtTrans.tar.gz`, which contains essential components for the protein language model [install.sh:4]().
2. **Path Configuration**: Appends the current directory to `PYTHONPATH` in `~/.bash_profile` to ensure modules are importable [install.sh:7-12]().
3. **Environment Creation**: Creates a Conda environment named `diso` using Python 3.9 [install.sh:15]().
4. **Dependency Installation**: Activates the environment and installs all packages listed in `requirements.txt` [install.sh:18-21]().

Sources: [install.sh:1-27]()

---

---

## Post-Installation Verification

### Verify Python Environment

Activate the newly created Conda environment:

```bash
conda activate diso
```

Check that Python and key packages are correctly installed:

```bash
python --version  # Should show Python 3.9
python -c "import torch; print(f'PyTorch: {torch.__version__}')"
python -c "import transformers; print(f'Transformers: {transformers.__version__}')"
```

Sources: [install.sh:15](), [requirements.txt:15,23]()

### Verify Directory Structure

Ensure that `ProtTrans.tar.gz` was successfully extracted by the script:

```bash
ls -d ProtTrans/
```

The root directory should now also contain the `models/` and `params/` directories necessary for running `run_disobind.py`.

Sources: [install.sh:4]()

---

## Troubleshooting Common Installation Issues

### Issue: ProtTrans Extraction Failed

**Problem**: The `ProtTrans` directory is missing after running `install.sh`.

**Solution**: Manually extract the archive:
```bash
tar -xzvf ./ProtTrans.tar.gz
```
Ensure you have sufficient disk space, as language model assets can be large.

Sources: [install.sh:4]()

### Issue: PYTHONPATH Not Updated

**Problem**: Importing Disobind modules results in `ModuleNotFoundError`.

**Solution**: The `install.sh` script attempts to update `~/.bash_profile` [install.sh:7-12](). If you are using `zsh`, you may need to manually add the path to `~/.zshrc`:
```bash
export PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:$(pwd)
```

### Issue: Dependency Conflicts

**Problem**: `pip install` fails due to version conflicts.

**Solution**: Disobind requires specific versions like `numpy==1.24.3` and `pandas==1.5.0`. Ensure you are installing into a clean `diso` environment as created by the script.

Sources: [requirements.txt:11,13](), [install.sh:15]()

---

## Next Steps

After successful installation:

1. **Quick Start**: Run a test prediction using the instructions in **1.2 Quick Start Guide**.
2. **GPU Setup**: If you have an NVIDIA GPU, verify that `torch.cuda.is_available()` returns `True` within the `diso` environment.
3. **Explore Data**: Review the `example/` folder to understand the input formats required by the system.

Sources: [install.sh:26-27]()

## Purpose and Scope

This guide provides a practical walkthrough for running your first Disobind predictions. It covers the essential steps from preparing input files to interpreting output predictions for binary protein complexes containing at least one intrinsically disordered region (IDR).

For detailed information about installation and environment setup, see [Installation and Setup](1.1). For comprehensive documentation on prediction options and parameters, see [Running Predictions](2). For output file formats and interpretation details, see [Output Files and Interpretation](2.4).

**Sources:** [README.md:1-129]()

---

## Prerequisites Check

Before running Disobind, verify your installation:

```bash
# Activate the conda environment
conda activate disobind

# Verify Python packages
python -c "import torch; import Bio; print('Dependencies OK')"

# Check model files exist
ls models/Epsilon_3_6/Version_0/
ls models/Epsilon_3_16/Version_2/
```

The Disobind models should be located in the `models/` directory with the following structure:

| Model Type | CG Level | Directory | Purpose |
|------------|----------|-----------|---------|
| Epsilon_3_6 | 10 | `models/Epsilon_3_6/Version_0/` | Interaction prediction (contact maps) |
| Epsilon_3_6 | 5 | `models/Epsilon_3_6/Version_1/` | Interaction prediction (contact maps) |
| Epsilon_3_6 | 1 | `models/Epsilon_3_6/Version_2/` | Interaction prediction (contact maps) |
| Epsilon_3_16 | 10 | `models/Epsilon_3_16/Version_0/` | Interface residue prediction |
| Epsilon_3_16 | 5 | `models/Epsilon_3_16/Version_1/` | Interface residue prediction |
| Epsilon_3_16 | 1 | `models/Epsilon_3_16/Version_2/` | Interface residue prediction |

**Sources:** [run_disobind.py:86-87](), [README.md:14-38]()

## Understanding Input Format

Disobind accepts protein pairs in CSV or FASTA format. Each entry represents one binary complex to predict.

### Input Format for Disobind Only (CSV)

For predictions using only Disobind (sequence-based):

```
UniProt_ID1,start1,end1,UniProt_ID2,start2,end2
```

**Example:**
```csv
P04273,95,193,P04273,95,192
```

This specifies a homodimer where:
- Protein 1: UniProt P04273, residues 95-193
- Protein 2: UniProt P04273, residues 95-192

### Input Format for Disobind+AF2 (CSV)

To combine Disobind predictions with AlphaFold2 structural information:

```
UniProt_ID1,start1,end1,UniProt_ID2,start2,end2,AF2_struct_file,AF2_json_file,chain1,chain2,offset1,offset2
```

**Example:**
```csv
P04273,95,193,P04273,95,193,./example/unrelaxed_model_4_multimer_v3_pred_4.pdb,./example/pae_model_4_multimer_v3_pred_4.json,B,C,0,0
```

### FASTA format

If proteins do not have a UniProt accession, use FASTA format:
```
>UniProt_ID1, start1, end1, AF2_struct_file_path, AF2_pae_file_path, chain1, offset1
Protein 1 Sequence
>UniProt_ID2, start2, end2, AF2_struct_file_path, AF2_pae_file_path, chain2, offset2
Protein 2 Sequence
```

**Important Constraints:**
- Protein 1 must be an IDR.
- Protein 2 may or may not be an IDR.
- Only binary complexes (AB) are supported. For non-binary complexes (ABC), convert them into binary pairs (AB, BC, AC).

**Sources:** [run_disobind.py:208-255](), [README.md:42-73](), [example/test.csv:1-2]()

---

## Running Your First Prediction

### Example 1: Basic Disobind Prediction

Use the provided example file `example/test.csv`. Run Disobind with default settings (interface prediction only, CG=1):

```bash
python run_disobind.py -i csv -f ./example/test.csv 
```

**Key Command-Line Options:**

| Flag | Default | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| `-i` | `csv` | Input file type (`csv` or `fasta`) |
| `-f` | Required | Path to the input file |
| `-o` | `output` | Output directory name |
| `-d` | `cpu` | Device: `cpu` or `cuda` |
| `-c` | `2` | Number of cores for downloading UniProt sequences |
| `-cm` | `False` | Predict inter-protein contact maps |
| `-cg` | `1` | Coarse-graining level: `0` (all), `1`, `5`, or `10` |

**Sources:** [run_disobind.py:126-161](), [README.md:76-93]()

---

## Understanding the Output

### Output Files

After running Disobind, the following files are generated in the output directory:

1. **CSV output file**: Contains residue-level interaction predictions.
2. **`Predictions.npy`**: Contains predictions for all input sequence fragment pairs in a nested dictionary.

### CSV Output Interpretation

| Protein1 | Residue1 | Protein2 | Residue2 |
|----------|----------|----------|----------|
| X1 | 10 | X2 | 40 |

- **Contact Map Prediction (`-cm`)**: Residue 10 in protein X1 interacts with residue 40 in protein X2.
- **Interface Prediction (Default)**: Residues in Protein1 (left) may interact with one or more residues in Protein2 (right).

**Sources:** [README.md:95-114]()

---

## Code Components Reference

The following diagram maps the main code entities involved in the prediction workflow:

**Disobind Class Structure and Workflow**

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Main Entry Point"

    subgraph "Input Processing"
        ReadCSV["read_csv_input()<br/>line 208-255"]
        GetUniIDs["get_unique_uni_ids()<br/>line 280-295"]
        DownloadSeqs["download_uniprot_seq()<br/>line 299-327"]
        ProcessPairs["process_input_pairs()<br/>line 333-368"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Embedding Generation"
        EmbClass["Embeddings class<br/>create_input_embeddings.py"]
        CreateEmb["create_embeddings()<br/>line 375-395"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Loading"
        LoadModel["load_model()<br/>line 399-429"]
        GetModel["get_model()<br/>src/models/get_model.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Prediction"
        Predict["predict()<br/>line 532-661"]
        GetInputTensors["get_input_tensors()<br/>line 475-529"]
    end
    
    subgraph "AlphaFold Integration"
        AfPredClass["AfPrediction class<br/>line 831-1166"]
        GetConfident["get_confident_interactions()<br/>line 1150-1166"]
    end
    
    RunScript --> DisobindClass
    DisobindClass --> ReadCSV
    ReadCSV --> ProcessPairs
    ProcessPairs --> GetUniIDs
    GetUniIDs --> DownloadSeqs
    ProcessPairs --> CreateEmb
    
    DisobindClass --> LoadModel
    LoadModel --> GetModel
    
    DisobindClass --> Predict
    Predict --> GetInputTensors
    
    Predict --> AfPredClass
    AfPredClass --> GetConfident
```

**Key Classes and Methods:**

| Class/Function | Location | Purpose |
|----------------|----------|---------|
| `Disobind` | [run_disobind.py:43-826]() | Main orchestrator class |
| `Disobind.forward()` | [run_disobind.py:108-122]() | Entry point for prediction pipeline |
| `Disobind.predict()` | [run_disobind.py:532-661]() | Runs models and generates predictions |
| `AfPrediction` | [run_disobind.py:831-1166]() | Processes AlphaFold2 structures |

**Sources:** [run_disobind.py:43-1166]()

---

## AlphaFold2 Integration Strategy

Disobind can combine sequence-based predictions with AlphaFold structural contacts to improve accuracy.

**Combination Strategy:**
Disobind and AF2 predictions are combined using an element-wise maximum operation in `Disobind.predict()` [run_disobind.py:619-643]().

**Confidence Filtering:**
The `AfPrediction` class filters structural contacts based on:
- **pLDDT**: Per-residue confidence [run_disobind.py:1118-1128]().
- **PAE**: Predicted Aligned Error [run_disobind.py:1130-1148]().

**Sources:** [run_disobind.py:831-1166](), [run_disobind.py:619-643]()

---

# Page: Running Predictions

# Running Predictions

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [example/test.csv](example/test.csv)
- [example/test.fasta](example/test.fasta)
- [run_disobind.py](run_disobind.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page provides a comprehensive guide to the main Disobind prediction system, focusing on the `run_disobind.py` script and its core classes. It covers the overall prediction workflow, key components, command-line usage, and how the system processes protein pairs to generate interaction predictions.

For detailed information about specific aspects of the prediction system:
- Input CSV/FASTA format and data preparation → see [Input Format and Preparation](#2.1)
- Different prediction tasks (interaction vs interface) and coarse-graining levels (1, 5, 10) → see [Prediction Tasks and Coarse-Graining](#2.2)
- Combining Disobind predictions with AlphaFold2/3 structural predictions → see [AlphaFold Integration](#2.3)
- Understanding and interpreting output CSV, NPY, and HDF5 files → see [Output Files and Interpretation](#2.4)

---

## Overview

The Disobind prediction system is implemented in [run_disobind.py:1-1217](). It takes protein pairs as input (where Protein 1 must be an IDR [run_disobind.py:5-5]()) and predicts their interaction interfaces and contact maps. The system can operate standalone or integrate with AlphaFold2/3 predictions to enhance accuracy.

**Key capabilities:**
- Predict inter-protein contact maps and interface residues [README.md:111-113]().
- Process binary complexes at multiple coarse-graining resolutions (1, 5, 10) [run_disobind.py:58-59]().
- Integrate AlphaFold structural predictions with confidence filtering (pLDDT and PAE) [run_disobind.py:73-76]().
- Support for both UniProt-based CSV inputs and raw sequence FASTA inputs [run_disobind.py:214-223]().
- Batch processing for multiple protein pairs with automated embedding generation [run_disobind.py:184-207]().

**Sources:** [run_disobind.py:1-82](), [README.md:1-129]()

---

## Main Prediction Workflow

The following diagram shows the complete end-to-end workflow for running Disobind predictions:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input["Input: CSV or FASTA file"]
    
    ProcessIn["process_input_file()<br/>[run_disobind.py:212-258]"]
    
    CheckCache{"UniProt sequences<br/>cached?"}
    
    DownloadSeq["download_uniprot_seq()<br/>[run_disobind.py:299-328]<br/>via get_uniprot_seq()"]

    ProcessPairs["process_input_pairs()<br/>[run_disobind.py:333-368]"]

    GetTasks["get_required_tasks()<br/>[run_disobind.py:130-165]"]

    CheckAF{"AlphaFold files<br/>provided?"}

    Input --> ProcessIn
    ProcessIn --> CheckCache
    CheckCache -->|"No"| DownloadSeq
```

**Sources:** [run_disobind.py:111-128](), [run_disobind.py:168-207](), [run_disobind.py:532-661]()

## Key Classes and Components

### Disobind Class

The `Disobind` class [run_disobind.py:44-826]() is the main orchestrator for the prediction workflow. It manages input parsing, sequence retrieval, embedding generation, and the inference loop.

**Class Structure:**

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Disobind {
        +str input_file
        +str input_type
        +int cores
        +bool predict_cmap
        +int required_cg
        +str output_dir
        +str device
        +float threshold
        +Dict predictions
        +Dict uniprot_seq
        +forward()
        +process_input_file()
        +download_uniprot_seq()
        +process_input_pairs()
        +create_embeddings()
        +get_required_tasks()
        +load_model()
        +predict()
        +get_input_tensors()
        +extract_model_output()
    }
    
    class AfPrediction {
        +str struct_file_path
        +str data_file_path
        +List chains
        +List offsets
        +float plddt_cutoff
        +float pae_cutoff
        +get_structure()
        +get_interaction_data()
        +apply_confidence_cutoffs()
        +get_confident_interactions()
    }
    
    class Embeddings {
        +str scope
        +str embedding_type
        +Dict uniprot_seq
        +str fasta_file
        +str emb_file
        +initialize()
    }
    
    Disobind --> AfPrediction : "instantiates for AF integration"
    Disobind --> Embeddings : "delegates embedding generation"
```

**Key Attributes:**

| Attribute | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `input_type` | str | - | "csv" or "fasta" [run_disobind.py:53]() |
| `predict_cmap` | bool | False | Whether to predict contact maps [run_disobind.py:57]() |
| `required_cg` | int | 1 | Coarse-graining level (0, 1, 5, 10) [run_disobind.py:59]() |
| `device` | str | "cpu" | Device for inference (cpu/cuda) [run_disobind.py:68]() |
| `threshold` | float | 0.5 | Probability threshold for binary contact [run_disobind.py:70]() |
| `plddt_threshold`| float | 70 | AlphaFold pLDDT cutoff [run_disobind.py:74]() |
| `pae_threshold` | float | 5 | AlphaFold PAE cutoff (Å) [run_disobind.py:76]() |

**Sources:** [run_disobind.py:44-108]()

### AfPrediction Class

The `AfPrediction` class [run_disobind.py:831-1174]() handles the extraction and processing of AlphaFold2/3 structural predictions. It parses PDB/CIF structure files and JSON confidence data to generate filtered contact predictions.

**Key Methods:**

| Method | Purpose | Line Reference |
|--------|---------|----------------|
| `get_structure()` | Parse PDB/CIF file using BioPython | [run_disobind.py:872-879]() |
| `get_interaction_data()` | Compute contact map, pLDDT, and PAE | [run_disobind.py:1099-1115]() |
| `apply_confidence_cutoffs()` | Filter by pLDDT ≥ 70 and PAE ≤ 5 | [run_disobind.py:1118-1128]() |
| `get_confident_interactions()` | Generate final confident contact map | [run_disobind.py:1150-1173]() |

**Sources:** [run_disobind.py:831-1174]()

---

## Command-Line Interface

### Basic Usage

The system is invoked via `run_disobind.py` with specific flags for input type and path.

```bash
python run_disobind.py -i csv -f ./example/test.csv
```

### Command-Line Arguments

| Flag | Long Form | Default | Description |
|------|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `-i` | `--input_type` | - | Input file type: `csv` or `fasta` [run_disobind.py:1181]() |
| `-f` | `--file` | - | Path to the input file [run_disobind.py:1185]() |
| `-c` | `--max_cores` | 2 | CPU cores for sequence downloads [run_disobind.py:1189]() |
| `-o` | `--output_dir` | "output" | Output directory name [run_disobind.py:1193]() |
| `-d` | `--device` | "cpu" | Device: `cpu` or `cuda` [run_disobind.py:1197]() |
| `-cm` | `--cmaps` | False | Predict inter-protein contact maps [run_disobind.py:1202]() |
| `-cg` | `--coarse` | 1 | CG resolution: 0 (all), 1, 5, 10 [run_disobind.py:1207]() |

**Sources:** [run_disobind.py:1177-1217](), [README.md:84-93]()

---

## Prediction Pipeline Stages

### Stage 1: Input Processing
The script supports two input modes [run_disobind.py:214-223]():
1. **CSV Mode:** Preferred for batch processing multiple UniProt-indexed pairs.
2. **FASTA Mode:** Used for custom sequences without UniProt accessions (limited to one pair at a time).

For details on file structures, see [Input Format and Preparation](#2.1).

### Stage 2: Sequence and Embedding Generation
If UniProt IDs are provided, the system downloads sequences in parallel using `Pool` [run_disobind.py:314-318](). It then uses the `Embeddings` class to generate ProtT5 embeddings, which are saved to a temporary HDF5 file (`p1_p2_test.h5`) [run_disobind.py:106, 388-395]().

### Stage 3: Model Inference
The `predict()` method [run_disobind.py:532-661]() iterates through requested tasks. For each task, it:
1. Loads the appropriate Epsilon_3 model version [run_disobind.py:399-429]().
2. Prepares input tensors (padding and coarse-graining) [run_disobind.py:475-529]().
3. Runs the forward pass to obtain probability maps [run_disobind.py:598-600]().

### Stage 4: AlphaFold Integration
If structural files are provided in the input, the system computes structural contacts and filters them by confidence scores (pLDDT and PAE). The final prediction is often the maximum of the Disobind sequence-based prediction and the AF2 structure-based prediction [run_disobind.py:632-633]().

For details, see [AlphaFold Integration](#2.3).

---

## Output Files and Interpretation

The system generates several output files in the specified directory:

| File | Format | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `Predictions.npy` | NumPy / Dict | Nested dictionary containing raw probability arrays and DataFrames for all tasks [run_disobind.py:126](). |
| `diso_{id}_{task}_cg{cg}.csv` | CSV | Residue-level interaction pairs exceeding the threshold [run_disobind.py:795-802](). |
| `UniProt_seq.json` | JSON | Cached protein sequences [run_disobind.py:108](). |

**Interpretation:**
- **Contact Map:** A value at `(i, j)` indicates the probability that residue `i` of Protein 1 interacts with residue `j` of Protein 2.
- **Interface:** The probability that a residue is part of the binding interface, regardless of the specific partner residue.

For detailed output schema, see [Output Files and Interpretation](#2.4).

**Sources:** [run_disobind.py:758-825](), [README.md:95-114]()

---

# Page: Input Format and Preparation

# Input Format and Preparation

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [example/output.tar.gz](example/output.tar.gz)
- [example/pae_model_4_multimer_v3_pred_4.json](example/pae_model_4_multimer_v3_pred_4.json)
- [example/test.csv](example/test.csv)
- [example/test.fasta](example/test.fasta)
- [example/unrelaxed_model_4_multimer_v3_pred_4.pdb](example/unrelaxed_model_4_multimer_v3_pred_4.pdb)
- [run_disobind.py](run_disobind.py)

</details>



This page describes how to prepare input data for Disobind predictions, including the CSV input format, UniProt ID requirements, sequence download procedures, and embedding generation. For information about running predictions and model configuration, see [Running Predictions](). For details on AlphaFold integration with predictions, see [AlphaFold Integration]().

## Overview

Disobind accepts protein pairs as input via a CSV file. Each row specifies one protein fragment pair for prediction. The system automatically downloads UniProt sequences, generates T5 embeddings, and prepares input tensors for the neural network. Input preparation is handled by the `Disobind` class in `run_disobind.py` [run_disobind.py:44-106]() and the `Embeddings` class in `dataset/create_input_embeddings.py` [dataset/create_input_embeddings.py:38-40]().

**Sources:** [README.md:42-64](), [run_disobind.py:44-106]()

## Input CSV Format

### Basic Format: Disobind Only

For standard Disobind predictions without AlphaFold integration, each CSV row contains 6 comma-separated fields [run_disobind.py:7-8]():

```
UniProt_ID1,start1,end1,UniProt_ID2,start2,end2
```

**Field Descriptions:**

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `UniProt_ID1` | String | UniProt accession for protein 1 (must be an IDR) |
| `start1` | Integer | Starting residue position in UniProt sequence for protein 1 |
| `end1` | Integer | Ending residue position in UniProt sequence for protein 1 |
| `UniProt_ID2` | String | UniProt accession for protein 2 (may or may not be an IDR) |
| `start2` | Integer | Starting residue position in UniProt sequence for protein 2 |
| `end2` | Integer | Ending residue position in UniProt sequence for protein 2 |

**Example:**
```csv
P04273,95,193,P04273,95,192
```

**Sources:** [README.md:48-58](), [run_disobind.py:208-255](), [example/test.csv:1]()

### Extended Format: Disobind + AlphaFold2/3

For combining Disobind predictions with AlphaFold structural predictions, each CSV row contains 12 comma-separated fields [run_disobind.py:9-10]():

```
UniProt_ID1,start1,end1,UniProt_ID2,start2,end2,AF2_struct_file_path,AF2_pae_file_path,chain1,chain2,offset1,offset2
```

**Additional Field Descriptions:**

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `AF2_struct_file_path` | String | Path to AlphaFold structure file (.pdb or .cif) |
| `AF2_pae_file_path` | String | Path to AlphaFold PAE JSON file |
| `chain1` | String | Chain ID in AF2 structure corresponding to protein 1 fragment |
| `chain2` | String | Chain ID in AF2 structure corresponding to protein 2 fragment |
| `offset1` | Integer | Residue position offset between AF2 structure and UniProt numbering for protein 1 |
| `offset2` | Integer | Residue position offset between AF2 structure and UniProt numbering for protein 2 |

**Offset Calculation:** The offset is the difference between the AF2 structure residue numbering and the UniProt residue numbering [README.md:63-65](). Set to 0 if the AF2 structure corresponds to the full UniProt sequence or the exact fragment specified.

**Example:**
```csv
P04273,95,193,P04273,95,193,./example/unrelaxed_model_4_multimer_v3_pred_4.pdb,./example/pae_model_4_multimer_v3_pred_4.json,B,C,0,0
```

**Sources:** [README.md:57-65](), [run_disobind.py:232-253](), [example/test.csv:2]()

## Input Requirements and Constraints

The following requirements and constraints apply to all input:

1. **Binary Complexes Only:** Disobind only processes binary (two-protein) complexes. For non-binary complexes ABC, create binary pairs: AB, BC, AC [README.md:43-44]().
2. **Protein 1 Must Be an IDR:** The first protein in each pair must be an intrinsically disordered region. Protein 2 may be ordered or disordered [README.md:45]().
3. **Interacting Pairs:** The input protein pair is assumed to be interacting. Disobind predicts *where* they interact, not *whether* they interact [README.md:44]().
4. **Valid UniProt IDs:** By default, CSV input expects proteins with UniProt accessions for sequence retrieval [README.md:49]().
5. **Alternative FASTA Input:** For proteins without UniProt accessions, the FASTA format can be used to provide sequences directly [README.md:50-51]().

**Sources:** [README.md:42-51](), [run_disobind.py:4-10]()

## Input Processing Pipeline

The following diagram shows the complete input processing workflow from CSV file to model-ready tensors:

**Diagram: Input Processing Workflow**

```mermaid

    ReadCSV["process_input_file()<br/>[run_disobind.py:212]"]
    ParseRows["Parse CSV Rows<br/>Extract UniProt IDs<br/>and Residue Ranges"]
    EntryDict["entry_ids List<br/>af_dict Dictionary"]

    GetUniqueIDs --> ParallelDownload
    ParallelDownload --> APICall

    UniSeqFile --> ProcessPairs

    ValidatePairs --> ProtPairs
    ProtPairs --> CreateFasta
    CreateFasta --> FastaFile
    
    FastaFile --> CheckEmb
    CheckEmb -->|No| GenEmb
    CheckEmb -->|Yes| LoadEmb
    
    GenEmb --> T5Script
    T5Script --> EmbFile
    EmbFile --> LoadEmb
    
    LoadEmb --> EmbDict

```

**Sources:** [run_disobind.py:111-207](), [run_disobind.py:212-368](), [run_disobind.py:475-529](), [dataset/create_input_embeddings.py:186-273]()

## CSV Parsing and Entry ID Format

The `process_input_file()` method (specifically for CSV type) parses the file and creates internal entry identifiers [run_disobind.py:212-255]():

```
UniID1:start1:end1--UniID2:start2:end2_0
```

The `_0` suffix indicates this is the first fragment pair for this combination. The method also constructs an `af_dict` dictionary to store AlphaFold-related information.

**Diagram: CSV Parsing and Data Structures**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "CSV Input"
        Row["P04273,95,193,P04273,95,192<br/>OR<br/>P04273,95,193,P04273,95,193,<br/>path/to/pdb,path/to/json,<br/>B,C,0,0"]
    end
    
    subgraph "read_csv() Processing"
        Split["Split by Comma<br/>Validate Length:<br/>6 fields or 12 fields"]
        ExtractFields["Extract Fields:<br/>uni_id1, start1, end1<br/>uni_id2, start2, end2<br/>(+AF2 fields if present)"]
        CreateID["Create Entry ID:<br/>entry_id = f'{uni_id1}:{start1}:{end1}--<br/>{uni_id2}:{start2}:{end2}_0'"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Structures"
        EntryList["entry_ids List<br/>['P04273:95:193--P04273:95:192_0']"]
        AFDict["af_dict Dictionary<br/>{<br/>  entry_id: {<br/>    'struct_file': path,<br/>    'json_file': path,<br/>    'required_chains': {<br/>      'chains': [chain1, chain2],<br/>      'offsets': [offset1, offset2]<br/>    }<br/>  }<br/>}"]
    end
    
    Row --> Split
    Split --> ExtractFields
    ExtractFields --> CreateID
    CreateID --> EntryList
    CreateID --> AFDict
```

**Sources:** [run_disobind.py:212-255]()

## UniProt Sequence Download

The system downloads UniProt sequences for all unique protein IDs in the input CSV. This process is parallelized using Python's `multiprocessing.Pool` for efficiency [run_disobind.py:261-278]().

### Sequence Download Process

1. **Extract Unique IDs:** The `get_unique_uni_ids()` method extracts all unique UniProt IDs from the entry list [run_disobind.py:280-295]().
2. **Parallel Download:** The `download_uniprot_seq()` method uses a multiprocessing pool to download sequences in parallel [run_disobind.py:299-327]().
3. **API Logic:** The `get_uniprot_seq()` function in `dataset/from_APIs_with_love.py` handles the HTTP requests to UniProt [dataset/from_APIs_with_love.py:10]().
4. **Caching:** Downloaded sequences are saved to `UniProt_seq.json` in the output directory to avoid re-downloading [run_disobind.py:108]().

**Sources:** [run_disobind.py:261-327](), [dataset/from_APIs_with_love.py:10-40]()

## FASTA File Generation

The `create_fasta_from_headers()` method generates FASTA files containing sequences for embedding generation [dataset/create_input_embeddings.py:186-235]().

### Global Scope (Default)

For global embeddings, the complete UniProt sequence is written to the FASTA file:

```
>P04273
MDSKGSSQKGSRLLLLLVVSNLLLCQGVVSTPVCPNGPGNCQVSLRDLFDRAVMVSHYIHDLSSEMFNEFDKRYAQGK...
```

**Sources:** [dataset/create_input_embeddings.py:207-210](), [run_disobind.py:66]()

## Embedding Generation

Disobind uses ProtT5 embeddings by default [run_disobind.py:64](). The embedding generation process involves calling external scripts from the ProtTrans library.

### Embedding Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    FastaInput["FASTA File<br/>p1_p2_test.fasta"]
    
    GetEmb["get_embeddings()<br/>[utility.py:155]"]
    CheckType{"embedding_type?"}
    
    T5["ProtT5_embeddings()<br/>[utility.py:342]"]
    
    ChangeDir["os.chdir(ProtTrans/Embedding/)"]
    CallScript["subprocess.call(['python',<br/>'prott5_embedder.py',<br/>'--input', fasta_file,<br/>'--output', emb_file])"]
    
    EmbFile["Embeddings HDF5 File<br/>p1_p2_test.h5<br/>Per-residue embeddings<br/>Shape: [L, 1024]"]
    
    LoadH5["h5py.File() Open<br/>get_global_embeddings()<br/>[create_input_embeddings.py:276]"]
    SliceEmb["Slice Embeddings<br/>emb[start-1:end]<br/>for Fragment"]
    
    EmbDicts["prot1_emb Dictionary<br/>prot2_emb Dictionary<br/>{entry_id: np.array}"]
    
    FastaInput --> GetEmb
    GetEmb --> CheckType
    CheckType -->|T5| T5
    
    T5 --> ChangeDir
    ChangeDir --> CallScript
    CallScript --> EmbFile
    
    EmbFile --> LoadH5
    LoadH5 --> SliceEmb
    SliceEmb --> EmbDicts
```

### Embedding Properties

| Property | Value | Description |
|----------|-------|-------------|
| Embedding Type | ProtT5 | Default, set in `Disobind` class [run_disobind.py:64]() |
| Dimensions | [L, 1024] | Per-residue embeddings, L = sequence length |
| Storage Format | HDF5 | Key = entry ID or UniProt ID, Value = embedding array |
| Scope | Global | Uses full sequence for context [run_disobind.py:66]() |

**Sources:** [dataset/create_input_embeddings.py:239-273](), [dataset/utility.py:342-372](), [run_disobind.py:64-66]()

## Input Tensor Preparation

After embeddings are loaded, they must be converted to model-ready tensors. This involves padding, coarse-graining, and creating masks.

### Tensor Preparation Steps

The `get_input_tensors()` method [run_disobind.py:475-529]() performs the following operations:

1. **Calculate Effective Length:** Compute post-coarse-graining dimensions [run_disobind.py:488-490]().
2. **Create Target Mask:** Initialize a binary mask of ones with shape `[1, num_res1, num_res2]` [run_disobind.py:492]().
3. **Convert to Tensors:** Convert numpy arrays to PyTorch tensors and add batch dimension [run_disobind.py:504-507]().
4. **Apply Padding and Coarse-Graining:** Call `prepare_input()` from `src/utils.py` to pad sequences to 100 residues and apply coarse-graining [run_disobind.py:510-525]().
5. **Move to Device:** Transfer tensors to specified device (CPU or CUDA) [run_disobind.py:527]().

**Sources:** [run_disobind.py:475-529](), [src/utils.py:10-40]()

## Batch Processing

Predictions are processed in batches to manage memory efficiently. The default batch size is 200 protein pairs [run_disobind.py:78]().

**Diagram: Batch Processing Loop**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["Start: get_predictions()<br/>[run_disobind.py:168]"]
    CalcBatch["Calculate Batch Ranges<br/>np.arange(0, total_pairs, batch_size)"]
    
    Loop{"More<br/>Batches?"}
    SelectBatch["Select Batch:<br/>batch = prot_pairs[start:end]"]
    CreateEmb["create_embeddings(batch)<br/>[run_disobind.py:375]"]
    
    Predict["predict(required_tasks, af_dict)<br/>[run_disobind.py:532]"]
    ProcessEntry["For Each Entry in Batch:<br/>- Load embeddings<br/>- Get input tensors<br/>- Run model inference"]
    
    UpdateDict["Update predictions Dictionary"]
    Cleanup["Remove Processed Files:<br/>rm emb_file, fasta_file"]
    
    SaveOutput["Save predictions.npy"]
    End["End"]
    
    Start --> CalcBatch
    CalcBatch --> Loop
    Loop -->|Yes| SelectBatch
    SelectBatch --> CreateEmb
    CreateEmb --> Predict
    Predict --> ProcessEntry
    ProcessEntry --> UpdateDict
    UpdateDict --> Cleanup
    Cleanup --> Loop
    Loop -->|No| SaveOutput
    SaveOutput --> End
```

**Sources:** [run_disobind.py:168-207](), [run_disobind.py:532-661]()

## Error Handling and Validation

The input processing pipeline includes several validation steps:

1. **CSV Format Validation** [run_disobind.py:228-242](): Verifies each row has exactly 6 or 12 fields.
2. **UniProt Download Validation** [run_disobind.py:320-324](): Checks if sequence length is non-zero.
3. **Sequence Availability** [run_disobind.py:362-366](): Skips pairs with missing UniProt sequences and logs a warning.
4. **Coarse-Graining Validation** [run_disobind.py:144-151](): Verifies CG value is in [0, 1, 5, 10] and warns about potential terminal residue loss.

**Sources:** [run_disobind.py:144-151](), [run_disobind.py:228-242](), [run_disobind.py:320-324](), [run_disobind.py:362-366]()
